summary: In this fiction excerpt from 'Book 3 — part 177', the narrator, Morgy, reflects on the ancient rainforest and modern horror, then tends to Steve, who has been drugged and beaten and is held in a room with Sarah. She works to rouse him by talking, slapping, and walking him by the window until his eyes focus. Steve asks whether she is okay, and she worries that Ramos may kill them both now that Alex Goddard has what he wanted, deciding not to share that fear with Steve.
one_line: Morgy tries to revive the drugged and battered Steve in a rainforest room while fearing Ramos and Alex Goddard's plans.
key_facts: The narrator describes the old fairy tales as taking place in a deep wood where evil could lurk unfettered.
The narrator states that the earth's forests no longer symbolize the unknowable dark within us.
The narrator, Steve and Sarah are marooned in a thousand-year-old forest where horror still lived.
Steve is wearing a shift, and his clothes hang from a hook on the door.
The narrator says she will slap Steve around if necessary to get him going and able to walk.
The narrator pulls Steve to his feet and drags him to the slatted window at the rear of the room.
It takes ten minutes of working on Steve before his eyelids begin to flutter.
Steve's first audible words are a timorous request: "Can I please lie down?"
Steve's first question after waking is "Morgy, are you okay?"
The narrator says "I'm going to be" in response to Steve's question about her well-being.
Steve grins with only half his face, and the narrator can tell even that hurts.
The narrator wonders whether Ramos will kill them both now that Alex Goddard has gotten everything he wanted.
The narrator decides not to share the possibility of being killed with Steve at this moment.
The narrator tells Steve, "Baby, just walk a little more" to flush the chemicals out of his brain.
